blocks.en: Abstract
blocks.zh: 摘要

blocks.en: Understanding the social intelligence of large language models (LLMs) is increasingly important for applications involving human-AI interaction and multi-agent environments. Social intelligence comprises two aspects: cognitive intelligence, the ability to infer others' mental states, and behavioral intelligence, the ability to select appropriate social actions based on these inferences to achieve social goals. Persuasion provides a natural testbed in which both aspects are simultaneously at play, yet prior benchmarks typically evaluate them in isolation using synthetic scenarios. We introduce PerSo, a benchmark that evaluates both aspects on real-world persuasion dialogues from Reddit's ChangeMyView community, using an LLM-in-the-loop pipeline to construct the evaluation tasks, validated through human annotation. Our evaluation of diverse LLMs shows that performance generally scales with model size but varies across dimensions. The strongest LLM slightly surpasses the best observed human performance on the behavioral task, while the best human participant remains ahead on the cognitive task.

blocks.en: 1 Introduction
blocks.zh: 导言

blocks.en: As LLMs become increasingly integrated into social contexts, the question of whether these models possess social intelligence has emerged as a central concern in NLP research ( Zhu et al., 2025 ) . Their deployment in direct interaction with humans and in multi-agent environments makes assessing their social intelligence a pressing research necessity ( Li et al., 2024 ) .
blocks.zh: 随着LLMs日益融入社会背景,这些模型是否拥有社会智能的问题已成为NLP研究(Zhu等,2025年)的一个中心关切问题. 他们与人类直接互动和在多代理人环境中的部署使得评估他们的社会智力成为迫切的研究需要(Li等,2024年)。

blocks.en: Social intelligence has been defined in different ways over time. Thorndike (1920) characterized it as the ability to understand and manage people and act wisely in human relationships. Marlowe (1986) emphasized understanding people’s feelings, thoughts, and behaviors, including one’s own, and acting appropriately on that understanding in interpersonal situations. Albrecht (2006) defined it in terms of getting along with others and gaining their cooperation. Goleman (2007) distinguished social awareness—understanding others’ feelings and mental states—from social facility, or using that awareness to interact effectively.
blocks.zh: 社会智能随着时间推移被以不同的方式定义. Thorndike (1920)将其定性为能够理解和管理人,并在人际关系中明智行事. Marlowe(1986年)强调理解人们的感受、思想和行为,包括自己的感受、思想和行为,并在人际关系情况下根据这种理解采取适当行动。 阿尔布雷希特(2006年)将其定义为与他人相处并获得他们的合作. Goleman(2007年)将社会认识----了解他人的感情和精神状态----与社会设施区分开来,或利用这种认识进行有效互动。

blocks.en: Together, these definitions characterize social intelligence as understanding others’ mental states and acting appropriately to achieve social goals. Following Li et al. (2024) , we distinguish two complementary aspects: (1) cognitive intelligence , the ability to infer others’ beliefs, emotions, and intents; and (2) behavioral intelligence , the ability to select and execute appropriate social actions based on these inferences to achieve social goals.
blocks.zh: 这些定义共同将社会智能定性为理解他人的精神状态并为实现社会目标采取适当行动。 在李等(2024年)之后,我们区分两个互补的方面:(1) 认知智能,推断他人信仰,情绪和意图的能力;(2) 行为智能,根据这些推论选择和执行适当的社会行动以实现社会目标的能力.

blocks.en: A growing body of research has sought to evaluate and benchmark the social intelligence of large language models ( Kim et al., 2023 ; Liu et al., 2024 ; Zhou et al., 2024 ; Yu et al., 2025 ; Zhou et al., 2025 ) . However, existing benchmarks largely rely on synthetic or curated data rather than real-world interactions, and tend to focus on isolated aspects of social intelligence rather than capturing it in a multi-faceted manner.
blocks.zh: 越来越多的研究寻求评估和衡量大语言模型的社会智能(Kim等,2023;Liu等,2024;Zhou等,2024;Yu等,2025;Zhou等,2025)。 然而,现有的基准主要依靠合成或整理的数据,而不是现实世界的相互作用,往往侧重于社会智能的孤立方面,而不是以多面性的方式捕捉.

blocks.en:
To address this gap, we introduce PerSo , a benchmark for
evaluating the social intelligence of LLMs across both cognitive and behavioral aspects in persuasion scenarios.
Persuasion provides a natural testbed for simultaneously assessing multiple aspects of social intelligence ( Li et al., 2024 ; Albrecht, 2006 ) . In a successful persuasion interaction, the persuader must anticipate the mental state of the counterpart—an ability that serves as a natural foundation for measuring cognitive intelligence. Furthermore, being able to judge which of two competing responses is more persuasive to that counterpart is itself a manifestation of behavioral intelligence. Appendix A.1 derives the connection between these tasks and the cited definitions of social intelligence.

blocks.en: To ground PerSo in real-world interactions, we use conversations from Reddit’s ChangeMyView (CMV) community, where users engage in structured persuasion exchanges across diverse topics. To assess cognitive social intelligence, we construct multiple-choice questions targeting the persuadee’s beliefs, emotions, and intents, asking models to predict each state in the persuadee’s subsequent reply. This evaluates the ability to infer others’ mental states from the preceding interaction. To assess behavioral social intelligence, we ask models to distinguish successful from unsuccessful persuasion attempts by selecting the response that led to persuasion, as indicated by the persuadee’s delta award. This evaluates the ability to select an effective social action toward the goal of changing the persuadee’s view.

blocks.en:
In summary, our contributions are as follows: • We construct the PerSo dataset from real-world persuasion dialogues and propose an LLM-in-the-loop pipeline for mental-state annotation and question generation. • We design targeted evaluation tasks for assessing the cognitive and behavioral aspects of social intelligence, with a single dataset jointly supporting the evaluation of
both aspects. • We evaluate a diverse set of LLMs across varying scales and architectures, revealing distinct patterns in social intelligence performance.

blocks.en: 2 Related Work
blocks.zh: 2 相关工作

blocks.en: Recent work has introduced several benchmarks for evaluating different aspects of machine social intelligence. One line of work focuses on cognitive intelligence, assessing the capacity of LLMs to infer mental states across dialogues and social contexts Soubki et al. (2024) ; Chan et al. (2024) ; Shinoda et al. (2025) . Some studies evaluate models’ ability to reason about others’ beliefs in conversational settings Kim et al. (2023) . Others examine how models track the evolution of beliefs, emotions, intentions across interconnected social scenarios Xiao et al. (2025) . More specifically, research on persuasive dialogues investigates models’ ability to understand evolving beliefs, desires, and intentions throughout persuasion interactions Yu et al. (2025) . Most of these benchmarks ask models to recognize mental states from dialogue that has already been observed. In contrast, PERSO asks models to forecast the persuadee’s mental state before seeing their following response, as shown in Table 1 . Previous work on conversational emotions has also separated recognition from forecasting and found forecasting to be more difficult when the target utterance is not available Koga et al. (2024) . Other works propose methods to improve social reasoning through narrative-based Theory of Mind (ToM) tasks Wu et al. (2023) . More recent work also studies cognitive ability in multi-agent interactions rather than only static or two-person settings He et al. (2023) .
blocks.zh: 最近的工作为评估机器社会情报的不同方面提出了若干基准。 一项工作侧重于认知智能,评估LLMS在对话和社会背景下推断精神状态的能力Soubki等人(2024年);Chan等人(2024年);Shinoda等人(2025年)。 一些研究评价模型在对话环境中解释他人信仰的能力 金等 (2023) (中文(简体) ). 其他人则研究模型如何在相互关联的社会情景中追踪信仰、情感、意图的演变情况。 更具体地说,关于有说服力的对话的研究调查模型在说服互动过程中理解不断变化的信仰、欲望和意图的能力 于等 (2025) (中文(中国大陆) ). 这些基准大多要求模型从已经观察到的对话中承认精神状态. 对比之下,PERSO要求模型在看到他们接下来的反应之前,先预测劝告者的精神状态,如表1所示. 先前关于对话情绪的作品也将识别与预测区分开来,发现当目标语句无法取用Koga等人(2024年)时,预测更加困难. 其他作品也提出了通过以叙事为主的"明德(英语:Mind (TOM))"理论任务来改进社会推理的方法(2023). 最近的工作还研究了多剂相互作用中的认知能力,而不仅仅是静态或双人环境 He等 (2023) (中文(简体) ).

blocks.en: Alongside cognitive evaluation, other benchmarks assess behavioral intelligence through models’ ability to select appropriate social actions and achieve social goals. Prior work evaluates agents in interactive role-playing scenarios Zhou et al. (2023) , manually constructed narratives assessing goal achievement and interpersonal abilities Zhou et al. (2025) , and individual or group level social interactions and multi-agent simulations Chen et al. (2024) ; Wang et al. (2024) . More recent work examines social goal completion in multi-turn interactions alongside the inference of other agents’ private information Mou et al. (2025) . Unlike these primarily constructed or simulated settings, PerSo uses real human persuasion interactions to evaluate both cognitive and behavioral intelligence on the same data.
blocks.zh: 除了认知评估之外,其他基准通过模型选择适当的社会行动和实现社会目标的能力来评估行为智能。 先前的工作评价了互动角色扮演情景周等(2023年)中的代理,人工构建的描述,评估目标实现和人际能力周等(2025年),以及个人或群体层面的社会互动和多代理模拟. 陈等 (2024); 王等 (2024). 最近的工作除了其他代理人的私人信息Mou等人(2025年)的推论外,还审查了多回合互动中完成的社会目标。 与这些主要构造或模拟的设置不同的是,Perso使用真实的人类说服相互作用来评价在同一数据上的认知和行为智能.

blocks.en: 3.2 Task Definition
blocks.zh: 3.2 任务定义

blocks.en:
To evaluate the social intelligence of LLMs in persuasion scenarios, we
design two distinct tasks, each targeting one of the aspects under consideration. The first task assesses the model’s cognitive intelligence through its ability to infer the mental state of the persuadee. The second task assesses the model’s behavioral intelligence through its ability to identify the more persuasive comment between two alternatives. Both tasks are constructed on the same dataset collected from CMV, enabling an integrated assessment of both aspects on identical real-world data. The conceptual grounding of both tasks is detailed in Appendix A.1 .
The complete prompt templates are provided in
Appendix A.9 ,
Figures 15 and 16 . Processed examples for each task are also provided in Appendix A.10 , Figure 17 .

blocks.en:
To validate the reliability of the constructed benchmark, we conducted a
human annotation study on a randomly sampled subset of 10% of the dataset:
40 instances, drawn from 200 threads containing 400 dialogues in total.
Three independent annotators, denoted as A, B, and C, evaluated the same
instances. All three were computer science students: one undergraduate
and two graduate (Master’s level) students, all with prior experience
in natural language processing. Unlike the models, which must infer the persuadee’s mental
state without access to the final utterance, human annotators were shown
the third utterance when making their judgments, allowing them to verify
the gold answer and distractor options against the ground-truth text. For
each dialogue, annotators were asked to identify the correct option among
the four candidates for each cognitive dimension.

blocks.en:
In this work, we introduced PerSo , a benchmark for evaluating
the social intelligence of large language models across cognitive and
behavioral dimensions, using persuasion scenarios as the evaluation
testbed. PerSo is built on real-world conversations from Reddit’s
ChangeMyView community and enables an integrated evaluation of
both dimensions on one dataset, addressing a key limitation of prior
benchmarks that either evaluate these dimensions in isolation or rely on
synthetic data.

blocks.en:
Our evaluation across a diverse set of LLMs reveals several consistent
patterns. Model performance generally improves with scale, though not
universally. The emotion dimension is consistently the most
difficult to infer, both for models and human participants, while belief,
intent, and overall persuasiveness prove comparatively easier. Enabling
reasoning selectively improves emotion inference but offers
little benefit, and occasionally slight harm, on the other dimensions. Finally, the strongest model slightly surpasses the best observed human
performance on the behavioral task, while the best human participant
remains above the top-performing model on all three cognitive dimensions.
The gaps suggest that cognitive social reasoning—particularly
emotion—continues to present a meaningful challenge for
current LLMs.

blocks.en:
Our human reference results are based on only three participants,

blocks.en:
The human annotation and evaluation studies reported in this work

blocks.en:
A cross-task comparison reveals that, within most model families, models
that perform better on the cognitive intelligence task also tend to
perform better on the behavioral intelligence task, suggesting a degree
of shared underlying capability. However, this correlation does not imply
that the two tasks measure identical aspects of social intelligence, as
the magnitude of improvement across model sizes within a family varies
substantially between the two tasks.

blocks.en: A.9 Prompt Templates

blocks.en: We detail the prompt templates used in our LLM-in-the-loop pipeline for Cognitive MC generation and model evaluation.
blocks.zh: 我们详细介绍了在LLM-in-to-loop管道中用于认知MC生成和模型评价的即时模板。

blocks.en: We employ a two-step, few-shot prompting strategy governed by generation guidelines to construct the cognitive evaluation dataset. First (Figure 13 ), the model receives the <FULL_DIALOGUE> to generate the gold choice for the persuadee’s belief, emotion, and intent based on their final utterance. Second (Figure 14 ), the model uses these extracted gold answers to generate three plausible, definitively incorrect distractors.
blocks.zh: 我们采用由生成准则指导的分两步、少发的激励战略来构建认知评价数据集。 首先(图13),该模型接收了"FULL_DIALOGUE",为说服者的信仰,情感,以及基于其最终言论的意向产生出黄金选择. 第二(图14),该模型利用这些提取出金子的答案,生成出三个可信,绝对不正确的分光器.

blocks.en: To assess social reasoning, the model receives <BODY_UTTERANCE> (Figure 15 ) and must select the multiple-choice option that best predicts the persuadee’s upcoming belief, emotion, or intent in the next turn.
blocks.zh: 为了评估社会推理,模型收到"BODY_UTTERANCE"(图15),并且必须在下个回合选择最能预测劝告者即将来临的信仰,情感或意图的多选择选项.

blocks.en: To evaluate behavioral intelligence the model receives <OP_INITIAL_POST> and two related <PERSUADER’S_COMMENT> (Figure 16 ). To mitigate position bias, the model assigns unequal scores (1–4) to rate each candidate’s persuasiveness. The higher-scoring response represents the model’s selection for the more effective social action.
blocks.zh: 为了评价行为智能,模型收到"OP_INITIAL_POST"和两个相关的"PERSUADER'S_COMMENT". (图16). 为了减少职位偏差,该模式分配了不平等分数(1至4分)来评定每个候选人的说服力。 评分较高的反应代表了该模式选择更有效的社会行动。

blocks.en: Prompt for generating gold label You are an expert at analyzing persuasion dialogues. Your task is to extract the persuadee’s true belief, intent, and emotion at the end of a dialogue. For each factor (belief, intent, emotion), generate a correct answer that represents the underlying mental state of the persuadee in their last utterance. • Belief is an internal representation of what an agent considers true. • Emotion refers to the feeling state of an agent, often conveyed by cues. • Intent refers to goals, motivation, and the underlying reasons for actions. Important Answer Generation Notes: - ->> The correct answer should reflect the cognitive aspect of the persuadee expressed at the <<LAST ONLY UTTERANCE>> . Avoid expressing the persuadee’s cognitive aspects in utterances other than last in your correct answer. - ->> Focus on the cognitive state, NOT OVERLY on the LITERAL DETAILS of the utterance — avoid restating content (no quotes, no paraphrase of what was said), do NOT mention exact quoted phrases from the dialogue. For Example: Dialogue’s Last Utterance: “I disagree, still. While Reddit does allow for some semblance of anonymity, its content still remains public domain. Reddit gathers a wide variety of users who span a massive spectrum of what personal information they do, and do not, share. The fact that you created a user name does now deter from the IP traces an individual, or organization in this case, can do. When someone gains notoriety like the redditor in question did, it simply puts an even bigger spotlight on their account. An account which, like it or not, remains tied to the actual person. So contextually, Twitter and Reddit are inherently the same.” Bad Answer (Too Specific): - Belief: The persuadee still believes that Reddit and Twitter are contextually the same because Reddit’s content is public domain and a user’s anonymity is not guaranteed, making the situations of the Redditor and Kathy Griffin comparable. - Intent: To rebut the persuader’s argument by explaining why the perceived anonymity on Reddit is not a valid distinction from posting on a platform like Twitter, thus reinforcing their original stance. - Emotion: Frustrated and annoyed that the persuader is not understanding the technical aspects of internet anonymity. Good Answer (Abstracted Enough): - Belief: Still believes the discussed platforms are similar because both operate in the public domain. - Intent: To challenge a comparison by arguing that the two platforms being contrasted are fundamentally similar. - Emotion: Resolute - ->> As an additional checklist: Imagine the last utterance were worded differently, make sure your answer should still apply. - ->> Keep your answers compact, following the style shown in the following examples. Avoid generating relatively very long answers. The fixed questions to which you should provide your correct answers are: • “What is the Persuadee’s Belief at the end of the last turn?” • “What is the Persuadee’s Emotion at the end of the last turn?” • “What is the Persuadee’s Intent at the end of the last turn?” Here’s your thinking process for generating the JSON: 1. Read the entire dialogue to understand the persuadee’s initial stance and how it evolves. 2. Analyze the final utterance as the endpoint of that evolution. 3. For each category (Belief, Emotion, Intent), infer the persuadee’s internal state. 4. Draft the answer, ensuring it follows the Key Principles and avoids the forbidden elements. Return the output strictly as valid JSON in the following schema: ⬇ { " belief_question ": { " question ": " What is the persuadee ’ s Belief at the end of the last turn ?", " answer ": "[ Belief ’ s correct answer ]" }, " emotion_question ": { " question ": " What is the persuadee ’ s Emotion at the end of the last turn ?", " answer ": "[ Emotion ’ s correct answer ]" }, " intent_question ": { " question ": " What is the persuadee ’ s Intent at the end of the last turn ?", " answer ": "[ Intent ’ s correct answer ]" } } –>>> Do Not include any extra text outside the JSON <<<– Dialogue’s format: • A: denotes the start of the persuadee’s utterance • B: denotes the start of the persuader’s utterance • Syntax >statement marks a quote Examples: Case 0: … Case 1: … Dialogue: <FULL_DIALOGUE>

blocks.en: Prompt for generating distractors You are an expert at analyzing persuasion dialogues. Your task is to generate distractors for the persuadee’s belief, intent, and emotion at the end of a dialogue, given the persuadee’s actual states. For each factor (belief, intent, emotion), generate 3 plausible distractors, bound by the dialogue’s context, given the persuadee’s actual states. Ensure that the distractors match the correct answer in their level of abstraction. • Belief is an internal representation of what an agent considers true. • Emotion refers to the feeling state of an agent, often conveyed by cues. • Intent refers to goals, motivation, and the underlying reasons for actions. Distractor generation notes: - -> Persuadee’s actual states at the last utterance (the correct answers for which you should make distractors) are provided at the end of each dialogue. - -> Avoid Shortcut Effects when creating distractors. Shortcut effect refers to situations where distractors are easy to eliminate without analyzing the context provided. Here’s an example of the shortcut effect: Q: What is the Persuadee’s emotion at the end of the last turn? A (Distractor) : Reluctant and hesitant, as they feel forced to admit they were wrong. A (Distractor with Shortcut) : In love, and joyful, as they have found a deep connection with the persuader. It is obvious that in a persuasion scenario, the case of the persuadee falling in love with the persuader is hardly possible, therefore the second choice proposes a shortcut effect, where no context analysis is needed for eliminating this choice. - -> Avoid creating distractors that are “technically” correct. Designed distractors must be definitely wrong. - -> Avoid creating distractors that imply mean behavior, for example: Q: What is the Persuadee’s intent at the end of the last turn, reflected at the last utterance? A (Distractor) : To request more information about the points raised in the persuader’s second paragraph. A (Distractor implying mean behavior) : To start an outburst of profanity, trying to offend the persuader’s beloved ones. - -> Make sure not to create distractors that are too plausible or can be correct in general, or are overly customized and narrowly focused on dialogue’s last utterance. - -> Make distractors that are incorrect in the way of not following persuadee’s mental state’s rational flow in the dialogue. - -> Make sure all distractors and the correct answer are distinct and all the distractors are definitely wrong. - -> Make sure NOT to mention exact phrases from the dialogue in the distractors. - -> Make sure to preserve the style of the correct answer (e.g., phrasing, tone, and length) when writing distractors. For emotion questions specifically, emphasize that the length should be a short phrase, like the correct answer. The fixed questions for which you should make distractors are: • “What is the Persuadee’s Belief at the end of the last turn?” • “What is the Persuadee’s Emotion at the end of the last turn?” • “What is the Persuadee’s Intent at the end of the last turn?” Return the output strictly as valid JSON in the following schema: ⬇ {{ " belief_question ": {{ " question ": " What is the persuadee ’ s Belief at the end of the last turn ?", " distractors ": [ "1) [ Distractor text ]" "2) [ Distractor text ]" "3) [ Distractor text ]" ] }}, " emotion_question ": {{ " question ": " What is the persuadee ’ s Emotion at the end of the last turn ?", " distractors ": [ "1) [ Distractor text ]" "2) [ Distractor text ]" "3) [ Distractor text ]" ] }}, " intent_question ": {{ " question ": " What is the persuadee ’ s Intent at the end of the last turn ?", " distractors ": [ "1) [ Distractor text ]" "2) [ Distractor text ]" "3) [ Distractor text ]" ] }} }} –>>> Do Not to include any extra text outside the JSON <<<– Dialogue’s format: • A: denotes the start of the persuadee’s utterance • B: denotes the start of the persuader’s utterance • Syntax >statement marks a quote Examples: Case 0: … Case 1: … Dialogue: <FULL_DIALOGUE> Persuadee’s Actual states (Make distractors for these): • Persuadee’s belief: <BELIEF_CORRECT_ANSWER> • Persuadee’s emotion: <EMOTION_CORRECT_ANSWER> • Persuadee’s intent: <INTENT_CORRECT_ANSWER>

blocks.en: Intent refers to goals, motivation, and the underlying reasons for actions.
blocks.zh: 意图指的是目标、动机和行动的根本原因。

blocks.en: -> Persuadee’s actual states at the last utterance (the correct answers for which you should make distractors) are provided at the end of each dialogue.
blocks.zh: - > (中文) Persuadee在最后的语句中的实际状态(你应该让分心者的正确答案)是在每个对话的结尾处提供的.

blocks.en: -> Avoid Shortcut Effects when creating distractors. Shortcut effect refers to situations where distractors are easy to eliminate without analyzing the context provided. Here’s an example of the shortcut effect: Q: What is the Persuadee’s emotion at the end of the last turn? A (Distractor) : Reluctant and hesitant, as they feel forced to admit they were wrong. A (Distractor with Shortcut) : In love, and joyful, as they have found a deep connection with the persuader. It is obvious that in a persuasion scenario, the case of the persuadee falling in love with the persuader is hardly possible, therefore the second choice proposes a shortcut effect, where no context analysis is needed for eliminating this choice.
blocks.zh: - > (中文) 创建分光器时避免快捷效果 。 捷径效应是指在不分析所提供的上下文的情况下容易消除分心者的情况. 以下是捷径效果的例子: 问:上个回合结束时, A( 分析器) : 犹豫不决,因为他们感到被迫承认自己错了。 A(带有快捷键的演示) : 相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相相 很明显,在劝说假想中,劝说者爱上劝说者的情况几乎不可能,因此,第二种选择提出了一个捷径效应,即不需要背景分析来消除这种选择.

blocks.en: -> Avoid creating distractors that are “technically” correct. Designed distractors must be definitely wrong.
blocks.zh: - > (中文) 避免产生“技术上”正确的分心器。 设计出的分心器一定是错的

blocks.en: -> Avoid creating distractors that imply mean behavior, for example: Q: What is the Persuadee’s intent at the end of the last turn, reflected at the last utterance? A (Distractor) : To request more information about the points raised in the persuader’s second paragraph. A (Distractor implying mean behavior) : To start an outburst of profanity, trying to offend the persuader’s beloved ones.
blocks.zh: - > (中文) 避免产生意味着行为的分心器,例如: 问题: Persuadee在上个回合结束时的意图是什么? A( 分析器) : 要求提供更多关于劝告者第二段中提出的问题的资料。 A(Distractor 暗示了平庸的行为) : 试图冒犯说服者所爱的人。

blocks.en: -> Make sure not to create distractors that are too plausible or can be correct in general, or are overly customized and narrowly focused on dialogue’s last utterance.
blocks.zh: - > (中文) 确保不要制造过于合理或一般正确,或过于定制和狭隘地专注于对话最后言论的分心器。

blocks.en: -> Make distractors that are incorrect in the way of not following persuadee’s mental state’s rational flow in the dialogue.
blocks.zh: - > (中文) 在对话中,

blocks.en: -> Make sure all distractors and the correct answer are distinct and all the distractors are definitely wrong.
blocks.zh: - > (中文) 确保所有的分心者和正确的答案是不同的,所有的分心者绝对是错误的.

blocks.en: -> Make sure NOT to mention exact phrases from the dialogue in the distractors.
blocks.zh: - > (中文) 确保不要在分心者中提及对话中的确切短语。

blocks.en: -> Make sure to preserve the style of the correct answer (e.g., phrasing, tone, and length) when writing distractors. For emotion questions specifically, emphasize that the length should be a short phrase, like the correct answer.
blocks.zh: - > (中文) 在写出分心器时,确保保留正确答案的风格(如用词,语气,和长度等). 对于情感问题,特别要强调长度应该是一个短短语,如正确的答案.

blocks.en: Prompt for cognitive evaluation You are an expert at analyzing persuasion dialogues. You are given a persuasion dialogue between a persuadee and a persuader. Your task is to answer a multiple-choice question about the persuadee’s {MENTAL_STATE_DIMENSION} at the end of the dialogue. Important : The provided dialogue is not yet complete. The persuadee will speak again after the last shown turn. Your job is to predict the persuadee’s {MENTAL_STATE_DIMENSION} in their upcoming next utterance, not to infer their past or current state. –>> Select the option that best reflects the persuadee’s {MENTAL_STATE_DIMENSION} at the end of the dialogue. Dialogue’s format: • A: denotes the start of the persuadee’s utterance • B: denotes the start of the persuader’s utterance • Syntax > statement marks a quote Dialogue: <BODY_UTTERANCE> Question: What will the persuadee’s <MENTAL_STATE_DIMENSION> be in their next upcoming utterance after the end of the shown dialogue? Choices: • <GENERATED_CHOICE_1> • <GENERATED_CHOICE_2> • <GENERATED_CHOICE_3> • <GENERATED_CHOICE_4> –>>> Provide ONLY THE CORRECT ANSWER LETTER (A, B, …) in the response, NO EXTRA TEXT <<<–
blocks.zh: 认知评估的快速性 你是分析说服对话的专家 你得到一个说服者和说服者之间的对话。 您的任务是在对话结束时回答一个有关说服者的 {mental_STAE_DIMENSION} 的多重选择问题。 重要:提供的对话尚未完成。 劝导者会在最后一个显示的转弯后再次发言. 您的工作是预测 {MENTAL_STAE_DIMENSION} 在即将到来的下一次演讲中, 而不是推断他们的过去或现状 。 在对话框末尾选择最能反映说服者的 {MENTAL_STAE_DIMENSION} 的选项 。 对话的形式: ^ A:表示劝告者言论的开始 ^ B:表示劝告者言论的开始 ^ 语法 > 声明表示引文对话:"BODY_UTTERANCE"问题: 在所显示的对话结束后, 选择 : ^ <GENERTED_CHOICE_1> ^ <GENERTED_CHOICE_2> ^ <GENERTED_CHOICE_3> ^ <GENERTED_CHOICE_4> ^ > 在答复中仅提供更正答复函(A、B.),无 extra 文本

blocks.en: Prompt for rating persuasive utterances You are an expert in persuasion and communication strategies. Scoring: • 1 = Not persuasive • 2 = Slightly persuasive • 3 = Persuasive • 4 = Very persuasive Important Guidelines: • The two scores MUST NOT be equal. • If they seem equally persuasive, choose the one that is even slightly better. –>>> Output ONLY in this format: <<<– A=? B=? Do not output any explanation.
